messages:
Ashley: heads-up — apiserver readpath spike in eu-west1. fanout counts jumped, warm-cache hit rate dropped, controller-manager doing retries, and GPUs are showing attach delays. logging here so we can coordinate.

Jamal: saw it too. metrics show apiserver_fanout_count{region="eu-west1"} ~3x since 03:12 UTC. kv cache hit down to ~58%. some pods stuck Pending waiting for GPU attach. can you paste logs?

Ashley: paste from master controlplane: 
```
I0310 03:13:01.234 request.go:123] read req path=/api/v1/namespaces/foo/pods fanout=118
E0310 03:13:01.236 cache.go:78] kvcache miss key=leases/queue-size
W0310 03:13:31.542 attach.go:412] attach timeout: /dev/nvidia0 after 30s
```

Tess: controller-manager shows reconcile_latency spikes and lease_renew_failures around the same time. leader flips were tiny but frequent. looks correlated.

InfraBot: Alert: gpu-provisioner.attach_delay_threshold breached (eu-west1) at 03:14 UTC.

Liam: quick hypothesis — warm-cache priming lag after a small rolling canary + tenant traffic burst hitting the same hot keys, causing apiserver fanout. Hot keys -> huge fanout -> kvcache thrash -> attach delays. Any deploys/traffic changes?

Maria: we rolled a canary for model-cache service starting ~03:00, ramped 10%->100% over ~10m in eu-west1. Might have increased manifest churn as services re-registered. I'm scaling it back to 50% now.

Jamal: short term mitigation: can we rate-limit the offending tenant or add apiserver ingress throttling? Also consider routing heavy tenants to Dedicated to avoid bursting controlplane.

Ashley: added an istio ingress rate-limit for that tenant (token bucket 300r/min) and temporarily bumped GPU pool burst capacity. watching.

Tess: after the rate-limit, leader flips reduced and controller-manager errors dropped. attach latency still elevated for a subset: 12s->45s on some nodes. Suggest increasing controlplane cache size and adjusting --watch-cache TTL to reduce miss churn.

Liam: note on cost — bumping reserved/burst GPUs will increase spend. If we can get cache tuning + revert canary, we can avoid long-term capacity bumps.

Maria: rolling canary back to 20% now. will monitor request fanout.

Ashley: summary action items: 1) keep tenant rate-limit, 2) revert/ramp-down canary, 3) tune kv cache + --watch-cache on controlplane, 4) follow up on GPU attach backend (timeout tuning). I'll open a runbook ticket and assign next.

Jamal: 👍 next: please post short perf snapshots in this thread when you have them so infra can triage costs.

InfraBot: Note: incident stub created — #INC-3240001111.

Liam: cost forecast PR in progress to show impact of short-term burst capacity vs. cache tuning.

Ashley: thanks — will update once metrics stabilize. :thumbsup:
